voice.refText: You wake up and discover you can pause time. 10 seconds once a day. At first, you use it for dumb things. You catch your falling coffee. You dodge your boss in the hallway.

lines.text: You check everything before it happens.
lines.say: [intimate, close, almost amused] You check everything before it happens.

lines.text: The bus. The result. Her dots.
lines.say: [close, hushed, a little wondering] The bus. The result. Her dots.

lines.text: And the glass.
lines.say: [a quick catch of breath] And the glass.

lines.text: It's still there.
lines.say: [hushed, disbelieving] It's still there.

lines.text: What if you saw sixty seconds into the future?
lines.say: [low, curious, slow] What if you saw sixty seconds into the future?

lines.text: You have one minute. You've always had one minute. You just never knew it.
lines.say: [slow, a smile in it, landing] You have one minute. You've always had one minute. You just never knew it.

lines.text: Never late again. Never wrong-footed.
lines.say: [close, hushed, a little wondering] Never late again. Never wrong-footed.

lines.text: You'll never be caught out again. That's the gift.
lines.say: [warm, a little too pleased] You'll never be caught out again. That's the gift.

lines.text: And nothing will ever be new again. Small price.
lines.say: [wry, offhand] And nothing will ever be new again. Small price.

lines.text: Everything you look at has a ghost. The same street, one minute on.
lines.say: [confiding, easy] Everything you look at has a ghost. The same street, one minute on.

lines.text: It shows what happens if you do nothing.
lines.say: [confiding, easy] It shows what happens if you do nothing.

lines.text: Move, and it redraws.
lines.say: [confiding, easy] Move, and it redraws.

lines.text: Only a minute. Past that, everyone's reaction has already changed it.
lines.say: [confiding, easy] Only a minute. Past that, everyone's reaction has already changed it.

lines.text: And there's no off switch.
lines.say: [flat, a beat late] And there's no off switch.

lines.text: But the minute's up. The real glass goes.
lines.say: [dry, amused] But the minute's up. The real glass goes.

lines.text: You catch it. The saucer goes instead.
lines.say: [dry, amused] You catch it. The saucer goes instead.

lines.text: Chai-wallah: Saucer is extra, boss.
lines.say: [gruff, deadpan street vendor] Saucer is extra, boss.

lines.text: Next day, the canteen. Cricket on the TV, and the TV has a ghost too.
lines.say: [quick, deadpan, amused] Next day, the canteen. Cricket on the TV, and the TV has a ghost too.

lines.text: Six.
lines.say: [deadpan, certain] Six.

lines.text: Friend: How did you know?
lines.say: [loud, amazed] How did you know?

lines.text: They stop watching with you.
lines.say: [quiet, a little sad, dry] They stop watching with you.

lines.text: The batter on that screen has it worse. The fastest balls reach him in under half a second.
lines.say: [quick, deadpan, amused] The batter on that screen has it worse. The fastest balls reach him in under half a second.

lines.text: So the best batters read the bowler's hand and arm before the ball is even let go, and get ready early.
lines.say: [quick, deadpan, amused] So the best batters read the bowler's hand and arm before the ball is even let go, and get ready early.

lines.text: They guess, from the body. You don't have to guess.
lines.say: [quick, deadpan, amused] They guess, from the body. You don't have to guess.

lines.text: And you're the only one in the room not watching.
lines.say: [quiet, rueful] And you're the only one in the room not watching.

lines.text: Your boss is typing. Well. His ghost is.
lines.say: [dry, amused] Your boss is typing. Well. His ghost is.

lines.text: You send the deck before he's even asked for it.
lines.say: [quick, deadpan, amused] You send the deck before he's even asked for it.

lines.text: Boss: Great. Since you're free...
lines.say: [cheerful, too eager] Great. Since you're free...

lines.text: Every morning, the platform plays twice.
lines.say: [hushed, awed] Every morning, the platform plays twice.

lines.text: You know which seat will be empty.
lines.say: [quick, deadpan, amused] You know which seat will be empty.

lines.text: So does the man who watched you walk to it.
lines.say: [dry, a beat late] So does the man who watched you walk to it.

lines.text: You saw a minute ahead and still arrived late. Seeing always does.
lines.say: [dry, then quieter] You saw a minute ahead and still arrived late. Seeing always does.

lines.text: What you see is already old. Your brain takes about a tenth of a second to process it.
lines.say: [hushed, curious, slow] What you see is already old. Your brain takes about a tenth of a second to process it.

lines.text: Even this hand is a little bit ago.
lines.say: [whispered, wondering] Even this hand is a little bit ago.

lines.text: There's a trick of the eye called the flash-lag illusion. A light flashes level with a moving dot, but the dot looks ahead of it.
lines.say: [hushed, curious, slow] There's a trick of the eye called the flash-lag illusion. A light flashes level with a moving dot, but the dot looks ahead of it.

lines.text: Some scientists think your brain guesses forward to cover the gap.
lines.say: [hushed, curious, slow] Some scientists think your brain guesses forward to cover the gap.

lines.text: Even that sliver makes now uncertain. Yours is a full minute.
lines.say: [slow, low, letting it land] Even that sliver makes now uncertain. Yours is a full minute.

lines.text: Sundays are grandfather's.
lines.say: [warm, fond] Sundays are grandfather's.

lines.text: And grandfather has one story.
lines.say: [warm, fond] And grandfather has one story.

lines.text: Grandpa: A borrowed bicycle, a wedding...
lines.say: [old, delighted with himself, a storyteller] A borrowed bicycle, a wedding...

lines.text: The bicycle. The wedding. The wrong bride's house. You've heard it all your life.
lines.say: [warm, fond] The bicycle. The wedding. The wrong bride's house. You've heard it all your life.

lines.text: This time, you hear the ending a minute early.
lines.say: [warm, fond] This time, you hear the ending a minute early.

lines.text: And you laugh exactly on time. Too exactly.
lines.say: [light, then a small doubt] And you laugh exactly on time. Too exactly.

lines.text: Mom calls you twice a day. You've started answering before she asks.
lines.say: [warm, light] Mom calls you twice a day. You've started answering before she asks.

lines.text: Yes, you ate. Yes, you'll sleep early. No, the result isn't out.
lines.say: [warm, light] Yes, you ate. Yes, you'll sleep early. No, the result isn't out.

lines.text: Mom: You know me too well.
lines.say: [warm, bustling] You know me too well.

lines.text: Mom: Are you okay?
lines.say: [warm, bustling] Are you okay?

lines.text: You saw this one coming too. You still don't have an answer.
lines.say: [soft, slow] You saw this one coming too. You still don't have an answer.

lines.text: At home, Mom has started stopping halfway through her sentences.
lines.say: [quiet, flat] At home, Mom has started stopping halfway through her sentences.

lines.text: Because you keep finishing them.
lines.say: [quiet, flat] Because you keep finishing them.

lines.text: So you try something that can't look back at you. Your cousin's coin. You call it ten times in a row.
lines.say: [sly, a little bitter, quick] So you try something that can't look back at you. Your cousin's coin. You call it ten times in a row.

lines.text: Cousin: Not playing with you.
lines.say: [sulky, young] Not playing with you.

lines.text: It works. Until the other person notices.
lines.say: [sly, quick] It works. Until the other person notices.

lines.text: At the office Diwali party, you can see every hand a minute before it's played.
lines.say: [sly, quick] At the office Diwali party, you can see every hand a minute before it's played.

lines.text: You bet. And they fold, because you bet.
lines.say: [sly, quick] You bet. And they fold, because you bet.

lines.text: They stop dealing you in.
lines.say: [sly, quick] They stop dealing you in.

lines.text: Two physics students, Doyne Farmer and Norman Packard, once built a computer to beat roulette, and later hid it in a shoe.
lines.say: [sly, quick] Two physics students, Doyne Farmer and Norman Packard, once built a computer to beat roulette, and later hid it in a shoe.

lines.text: Farmer says it gave them about a twenty percent edge over the house. But the hardware kept failing.
lines.say: [sly, quick] Farmer says it gave them about a twenty percent edge over the house. But the hardware kept failing.

lines.text: Your hardware never fails. It's everyone else that changes.
lines.say: [dry, then quieter] Your hardware never fails. It's everyone else that changes.

lines.text: So far you've acted as if seeing it means knowing it.
lines.say: [low, flat, slow] So far you've acted as if seeing it means knowing it.

lines.text: She turns at your voice. And knocks the pan.
lines.say: [quick, then a drop] She turns at your voice. And knocks the pan.

lines.text: Her hand is fine. She doesn't speak to you again that evening.
lines.say: [flat, very quiet] Her hand is fine. She doesn't speak to you again that evening.

lines.text: Sociologists have a name for a forecast that stops itself coming true: a self-defeating prophecy.
lines.say: [low, flat, slow] Sociologists have a name for a forecast that stops itself coming true: a self-defeating prophecy.

lines.text: That's all the ghost ever was. Not the future. A rumour about a world where you stood still.
lines.say: [slow, low, certain] That's all the ghost ever was. Not the future. A rumour about a world where you stood still.

lines.text: Every Sunday since, you've heard the bicycle story twice. Once a minute early. Once on time.
lines.say: [quiet, close] Every Sunday since, you've heard the bicycle story twice. Once a minute early. Once on time.

lines.text: This time you laugh one second early.
lines.say: [quiet, tense] This time you laugh one second early.

lines.text: Grandpa: You've heard it.
lines.say: [old, delighted with himself, a storyteller] You've heard it.

lines.text: He does not finish.
lines.say: [almost a whisper] He does not finish.

lines.text: Later, he tells it to your cousin instead. You listen from the kitchen.
lines.say: [quiet, close] Later, he tells it to your cousin instead. You listen from the kitchen.

lines.text: Grandpa wants to see your college. His first ride on the metro.
lines.say: [tight, fast, urgent] Grandpa wants to see your college. His first ride on the metro.

lines.text: Grandpa: So many people!
lines.say: [old, delighted with himself, a storyteller] So many people!

lines.text: You steer him to the door you saw. In the ghost, he follows your hand, and the crowd takes him down at the gap.
lines.say: [tight, fast, urgent] You steer him to the door you saw. In the ghost, he follows your hand, and the crowd takes him down at the gap.

lines.text: You pull him left. It redraws. Worse.
lines.say: [fast, breathless] You pull him left. It redraws. Worse.

lines.text: You call his name. He turns to your voice, and steps into it.
lines.say: [fast, breaking] You call his name. He turns to your voice, and steps into it.

lines.text: Every move you make, he follows. And the minute moves with him.
lines.say: [tight, low] Every move you make, he follows. And the minute moves with him.

lines.text: In Japan, the bullet train lines have their own quake sensors. When the first tremor warns of shaking to come, they cut the power and the train brakes itself.
lines.say: [steady, low] In Japan, the bullet train lines have their own quake sensors. When the first tremor warns of shaking to come, they cut the power and the train brakes itself.

lines.text: That's what a little future is for. Not a winning hand. A stop.
lines.say: [warm, steady] That's what a little future is for. Not a winning hand. A stop.

lines.text: A weather scientist, Edward Lorenz, once reran a computer weather model with one number rounded off, and got a completely different forecast.
lines.say: [steady, low] A weather scientist, Edward Lorenz, once reran a computer weather model with one number rounded off, and got a completely different forecast.

lines.text: Tiny changes don't stay tiny.
lines.say: [steady, low] Tiny changes don't stay tiny.

lines.text: A ghost of next week would be rumour on rumour. One minute is enough.
lines.say: [steady, low] A ghost of next week would be rumour on rumour. One minute is enough.

lines.text: Grandpa: Did I ever tell you...
lines.say: [old, delighted with himself, a storyteller] Did I ever tell you...

lines.text: Watch him, or hear him?
lines.say: [almost a whisper, close] Watch him, or hear him?

lines.text: Grandpa: ...the wrong bride's house!
lines.say: [old, delighted with himself, a storyteller] ...the wrong bride's house!

lines.text: You laugh late. Loud. With your cousin.
lines.say: [warm, bright, a laugh in it] You laugh late. Loud. With your cousin.

lines.text: Your dopamine cells fire for a reward better than you expected. For one you saw coming, they stay flat.
lines.say: [warm, opening up] Your dopamine cells fire for a reward better than you expected. For one you saw coming, they stay flat.

lines.text: Being caught out was the gift.
lines.say: [slow, warm, landing] Being caught out was the gift.

lines.text: The ghost never gave you a new sense. It turned up one you already had, until it drowned out the thing it was for.
lines.say: [warm, opening up] The ghost never gave you a new sense. It turned up one you already had, until it drowned out the thing it was for.

lines.text: Friday. The result is out. Her dots are typing.
lines.say: [quiet, sure, warm] Friday. The result is out. Her dots are typing.

lines.text: You let them.
lines.say: [soft, sure] You let them.

lines.text: The bus comes when it comes.
lines.say: [easy, unhurried] The bus comes when it comes.

lines.text: You have one minute. You always had.
lines.say: [hushed, warm, final] You have one minute. You always had.
